tr: Hello, I'd like to order some flowers for an awards dinner at my company next Friday. We'll have twelve tables, so I need twelve arrangements.
Certainly. We have several options. Most clients choose our spring mix, which is forty dollars per arrangement.
That sounds nice, but they can't be too tall. People need to see each other across the table.
Of course. I can make them short and wide. Could you stop by the shop tomorrow? I'll have a sample ready for you to look at.
I'm in meetings all day, but I can come on Thursday morning.
Hi, Ana. My laptop screen keeps flickering, and I have a presentation to the board at two o'clock. Can you take a look at it?
Sure, but I'm in the middle of updating the server. It might be an hour before I can get to it.
That could be cutting it close.
Tell you what. There's a spare laptop in the IT cabinet. Sign it out on the sheet by the door, and you can use it for the presentation. Just copy your files to the shared folder first.
Perfect. I'll do that right now.
Julia, Amir, the trade show in Toronto starts in two weeks. How are preparations for our booth going?
The banners came back from the printer yesterday, and they look great. But we have only half the product samples we need.
That's because the factory ran behind schedule. They said the rest would ship by Monday.
Monday is too late if they're sent by sea. Could they be sent by air instead?
Yes, but it'll cost about six hundred dollars more.
We don't have a choice. We can't show up at the biggest event of the year without samples. I'll approve the extra charge.
Thanks. I'll update the shipping form.
Good afternoon, Regency Travel. This is Hana speaking.
Hi, Hana. It's Victor Okoye. You booked my hotel in Madrid for the fifth through the eighth, but the conference has been extended by a day.
So you'd like to stay until the ninth? Let me check. I'm sorry, but the hotel's fully booked that night.
Hmm. Is there anything else close to the conference center?
Yes, the Plaza Sol is just a block away. You could move there for the last night, or stay there for the whole trip.
I'd rather not change hotels. Please switch the whole reservation.
All right. I'll e-mail the new confirmation shortly.
Mr. Boyd, this is Helen in apartment 4C. The heater in my bedroom has stopped working, and it's been very cold at night.
I'm sorry to hear that. Our maintenance worker is off today, but he'll be back tomorrow. Would you be home around ten in the morning?
No, I work until six. But I can leave a key at the front office.
That works. In the meantime, I have a portable heater in the storage room. I can bring it up for you this evening.
Welcome to QuickPrint. How can I help you?
I need five hundred business cards. I just started my own accounting firm.
Congratulations! Do you have a design ready, or would you like to use one of our templates?
I have a logo, but that's about it.
No problem. Our designer, Sam, can put together a layout for you. Standard turnaround is five business days.
I'm speaking at a networking event on Saturday.
Ah. In that case, we can do it by Friday for an extra twenty-five dollars.
Hi, Mr. Nakamura. It's Paula Reed from Lumen Pharmaceuticals. We enjoyed reading your application for the research assistant position, and we'd like to invite you in for an interview.
That's great news. Thank you. When would you like me to come in?
We're seeing candidates next Tuesday and Wednesday. Do you have a preference?
Tuesday would be better. I'm giving a presentation at my university on Wednesday.
Fine. Let's say Tuesday at eleven. Could you bring a copy of your transcript? And please come to the main lobby and ask for me.
Good morning, Eastside Dental. This is Leo.
Hi, I have a checkup at three this afternoon, but I'm stuck at work. Could I come in later today?
Let me look. Dr. Malik is booked until five, and we close at five-thirty. How about tomorrow at nine?
That works. Is there a charge for changing it on the same day?
Normally there's a twenty-dollar fee, but since this is your first time, I won't charge you. I'll send you a text message with the new time.
Rick, I've been looking at quotes for our company's fiftieth anniversary party. The Grand Ballroom will cost eleven thousand dollars.
That's way over budget. What about holding it here at the office?
We'd have to rent tables and hire a caterer, but it'd cost about half as much. The roof terrace could hold everybody.
I don't know. What if it rains in September?
The terrace has a retractable cover. It was installed in the spring.
Then it's settled. Tara, could you check that the date is available? And I'll ask the finance department to release a deposit.
Grace, did you see the customer comments on the new self-checkout machines?
I did. A lot of people say they can't scan fresh produce easily.
That's what I've noticed, too. The lines are actually longer than they were last month.
Well, we did spend a fortune on those machines.
True, but we can improve things. What if we put an employee next to the machines during busy hours to help people?
I could move Tim from the bakery on weekends. Let's try that for a month and see how it goes.
Lucas, we need to be at the client's office near Central Station by ten tomorrow. Which train should we take?
Well, the walk from the station takes about twenty minutes, so we'd better arrive by nine-thirty.
You're right. I'd like some extra time to go over the slides, too.
OK. I'll buy the tickets online tonight. Are you going to bring the printed contracts, or should I?
I'll take care of those. I just have to get them signed by Ms. Burke first.

tr: You've reached the offices of Parkview Medical Group. Our offices are closed for the Labor Day holiday and will reopen on Tuesday at eight o'clock. If you'd like to make an appointment, please call back during regular business hours, or book online through our Web site. If you need a prescription refilled, please contact your pharmacy directly. If this is an emergency, hang up and dial your local emergency number. Thank you for calling Parkview Medical Group.

May I have your attention, please? This is an announcement for all staff on the fifth floor. As you were told in Monday's e-mail, today's fire drill will begin at two o'clock. When the alarm sounds, please stop your work and walk to the nearest stairway. Do not use the elevators. Once you're outside, go to the parking lot across the street and find your department leader, who'll have a list of names. The drill should take about twenty minutes. If you have visitors in the building, please make sure that they leave with you.

Welcome to Sweet Valley Chocolate. I'm Hiro, and I'll be taking you through our factory today. We make about ten tons of chocolate here every day, and most of the work is still done by hand. Before we enter the production area, there are a couple of things you need to do. For health reasons, everyone has to wash their hands and put on a hair net. You'll find these in the room on your left. And I'm afraid that photographs aren't allowed inside, since some of our recipes are secret. At the end of the tour, you'll get to taste our newest flavor, which goes on sale next month.

All right, the last item on today's agenda is our work-from-home policy. Starting in March, all employees will be allowed to work remotely two days a week. A lot of you have asked for this, and we're happy to offer it. But I want to be clear. The client service team has to have someone on-site at all times. Now, your managers will be working out those schedules next week. I've been told there have been some concerns about internet costs at home. The company will pay a monthly allowance of thirty dollars. You'll find the details in the employee handbook.

In local business news, Ashford Airlines announced this morning that it'll be merging with its smaller rival, Blue Coast Air. The new company will keep the Ashford name and will become the third-largest carrier in the region. Company officials say that passengers won't see any changes to ticket prices or routes this year. However, the two airlines' frequent flyer programs will be combined by next summer. Shares in Ashford rose six percent on the news. Coming up after the break, we'll talk with chef Rosa Mendez about her new cookbook.

Good morning, Mr. Farah. This is Nina from Oakline Furniture calling about the dining table you ordered. It was supposed to be delivered on Friday, but I'm afraid the manufacturer has run out of the walnut finish. They expect more in about three weeks. We do have the same table in dark oak, and that one's in our warehouse. And it's a more expensive finish. If you'd like that one instead, I'd be glad to deliver it this Friday at the original price. Please give me a call back when you've decided. My direct line is 555-0187.

Welcome to Introduction to Digital Photography. Over the next six weeks, you'll learn how to get the most out of your camera. Today we'll start with light, which is the most important part of any picture. Please take out the handout I've just given you. It shows the same scene at three different times of day. Notice how much the colors change. Next week, we'll be meeting at Riverside Park rather than here in the classroom, so that you can practice outdoors. Be sure to bring a fully charged battery, because there's nowhere to plug anything in.

Is your home too busy to keep clean? Let the professionals at Sparkle Home Services take care of it. For over ten years, we've been helping families across the Tri-County area with weekly and monthly cleaning. All our cleaners are fully trained, and we use only products that are safe for children and pets. Right now, first-time customers can get fifty percent off their first cleaning. Book before the end of the month by calling us or by using our mobile app. Sparkle Home Services. We do the dirty work, so you don't have to.

Good afternoon, everyone. I've got an update on the Greenfield Street Fair, which we'd planned to hold outdoors this weekend. Since there's a chance of heavy rain, we've decided not to open on that day. The fair will take place only on the following day. As a result, vendors will have less time to sell, so the city has agreed to return half of everyone's booth fees. Performers should check with Omar to confirm their new stage times. Also, we still need a few people to help with setup on Friday. If you're available, please add your name to the sheet by the door.

Welcome back from lunch, everyone. I hope you enjoyed the sandwiches. Before we continue, I have a small change to this afternoon's schedule. Our speaker for the two o'clock session, Lisa Wong, has been delayed at the airport, so her session will switch places with the one that's right after it. That means that I'll be speaking at two o'clock instead. Also, I noticed that a few people haven't turned in their feedback forms from this morning. Please leave them on the table at the back of the room. Thank you. And now, let's begin.

Local Firm Turns Coffee Waste into Fuel

BRISTOL — A small company in Bristol has found a new use for a very common form of waste. Each week, GroundUp Energy collects used coffee grounds from about 300 cafés across the city and presses them into logs that can be burned in stoves and fireplaces.

"The logs burn hotter and longer than wood," said founder Tessa Lowe, who came up with the idea while working as a café manager. "And they cost about the same."

Started three years ago with just two employees, GroundUp now has 18. It sold 40,000 packs of logs last year through hardware stores, and Ms. Lowe expects that figure to double when the company begins selling in Scotland next spring.

The group, led by retired teacher Moana Tait, raised more than $800,000 over four years to buy and restore the 1920s building. — [2] — Volunteers spent hundreds of hours repairing the plaster ceiling and the original wooden seats.

Unlike most modern cinemas, the Regal has only one screen. It shows classic films as well as new releases from New Zealand directors. — [3] — Ticket prices are kept low, and the cinema is run almost entirely by volunteers.

"We didn't want it to become just another parking lot," said Ms. Tait. — [4] — The cinema now sells about 1,500 tickets a week, and the owners of nearby restaurants say that their business has increased as well.
